target_customer: Urban Mexican consumers who order groceries online for delivery in under two hours
problem: Most grocery shopping in Latin America remains offline and supply chains are long and wasteful; fresh produce is costly and slow to reach consumers.
business_model: Full stack online grocer: owns inventory, buys direct from producers, delivers from micro-fulfillment centers, with later buy now pay later and electronics categories

founders.name: David Eduardo Arrambide Montemayor
education: Stanford (described as Stanford-educated engineer by TechCrunch; degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page.

founders.name: Maurizio Calo Caligaris
prior_employers: Stanford AI Lab (deep learning researcher under Andrew Ng)
education: Stanford (instructor and TA in the CS department; degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page, which also calls him a math olympic medalist.

competitors.name: Cornershop
competitors.what: Grocery delivery marketplace in Mexico and Chile where shoppers buy from existing stores
competitors.traction_then: Active in Mexico and Chile, acquired by Walmart in 2018
competitors.funding_then: About 31.7M raised through 2017 including a 21M round in May 2017 (Endeavor account via search summary); Walmart agreed to buy it for 225M in September 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard ecommerce and logistics software with hard operations parts: demand forecasting, inventory and micro-fulfillment centers.

defensibility.rationale: Direct sourcing and dark store density give scale advantages, but groceries are low switching cost and well funded rivals existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Walmart bought Cornershop in 2018 and large players kept expanding; Calii itself was not acquired as of the last news found.

market_need_then: The company says about 95 percent of grocery shopping in LatAm was offline; the pandemic later raised online grocery use. Walmart paid 225M for Cornershop in 2018, signaling demand. Spend at March 2019 itself not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses calii.com, which redirects to app.calii.com.

brand_strength.rationale: No sources on the name's meaning or brand identity were found; search for the name mostly returns unrelated Cali and California results, which hints at confusability.

pivots.to: Broader marketplace with electronics, appliances, a 40,000 item Market and Calii Pay buy now pay later
pivots.why: Announced with the Series A as expansion plans, not a documented pivot.

outcome_analysis: Calii launched in Monterrey in March 2019, tested the model for two years and reported more than 2,000 daily orders and threefold revenue growth when it raised a 22.5 million dollar Series A in January 2022, taking total funding to nearly 35 million. No later round or exit was found, and quick grocery delivery proved hard globally, so its current health is unknown.
notes: Total raised of nearly 35M (TechCrunch) exceeds the 22.5M Series A by about 12.5M; Caplight lists a 12.4M round with Base10 and Y Combinator dated 2019-03, unverified single aggregator so not recorded as a round. Calii site redirected and was not opened. Team size 750 on the YC page is a directory figure while TechCrunch said 250 in January 2022. YC lists batch Summer 2018 but founding year 2019 and launch March 2019. Rappi Turbo, Jokr and Jus. named in 2022 are later entrants and are not listed. Cornershop funding figure comes from a search summary of an Endeavor page and a TechCrunch May 2017 article, not opened. No layoff or shutdown news found.
